title: Global and Local Inversions
spaceBreakdown:
- loop index `i` (int): O(1)
- no containers, recursion, or auxiliary arrays allocated
- not counted: input `nums`
approach: Every local inversion is automatically a global inversion, so the two counts are equal exactly when every global inversion is also local - i.e., no element is "too far" from its sorted position. Because `nums` is a permutation of `[0, n-1]`, the value `v` belongs at index `v`. If any `nums[i]` differs from `i` by more than 1, then some smaller value is displaced far to the right, creating a global inversion that is not local. So we just scan once and reject if `|nums[i] - i| > 1`.
hints: Every local inversion is automatically a global inversion. So for the two counts to be equal, what must be true about every global inversion that is NOT a local one - and where must each value sit relative to its position in the sorted permutation?
Check whether any element sits more than one index away from its value. In `[1,2,0]`, the value `0` is at index `2` but belongs at index `0` - distance `2` - so a non-local global inversion exists.

**Smallest input** - only one element, no pairs to compare.
`Input: nums = [0]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: special-casing `n < 2` to return `false` → returns `false`

**Already sorted** - every element is exactly at home, zero inversions of either kind.
`Input: nums = [0,1,2]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning `false` whenever `nums[i] != i` (forbidding any swap) → returns `false`

**Reverse sorted** - the largest value is at the front, far from home.
`Input: nums = [2,1,0]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: only checking `nums[i] - i > 1` (one direction, no abs) → at i=0, `2-0=2>1` catches it, but at i=2 `0-2=-2` is ignored; on `[1,2,0]` this bug returns `true` instead of `false`

**Value displaced backward only** - no element is too large, but one is too small.
`Input: nums = [1,2,0]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking only `nums[i] - i > 1` without the reverse direction → `0-2=-2` is not `>1`, returns `true`

followUps.q: What if `nums` may contain duplicates (no longer a strict permutation)?
followUps.a: The `|nums[i]-i| ≤ 1` invariant no longer holds, so count global inversions with a Fenwick tree over values and local inversions with a linear scan, then compare. Time becomes O(n log n), space O(n) for the BIT.

followUps.q: What if you must return the exact difference `global - local` instead of a boolean?
followUps.a: When the invariant holds the difference is `0`; otherwise compute both counts (Fenwick for global, linear for local) and subtract. Time O(n log n), space O(n).

followUps.q: What if elements arrive in a stream and you must report `false` as soon as the property breaks?
followUps.a: Keep the running maximum of `nums[0..i-2]`; when the next value arrives at index `i`, if that max exceeds `nums[i]`, a non-local global inversion exists. Time O(n), space O(1).
